subject: Cloud Computing
title: Azure's Enterprise Strategy
description: A short lesson to help you apply Azure's Enterprise Strategy.

hook.text: Microsoft was late to cloud. But it had something AWS didn't: relationships with every enterprise IT department.

buildup.text: Azure launched in 2010. Microsoft bundled it with existing Office and Windows enterprise contracts.

discovery.text: Enterprises already paying for Microsoft products got Azure discounts. Switching was the easy choice.

twist.text: Azure's strategy wasn't better tech — it was better sales. Enterprise trust took decades to build.

climax.text: Azure now holds about 24% of the cloud market and is the fastest-growing major cloud platform.

punchline.text: Azure won enterprises not with tech but with trust.

quiz.question: How did Microsoft Azure gain enterprise market share despite launching late?
options: By leveraging existing enterprise relationships and bundling with Microsoft products
By offering the lowest prices in the cloud market
By acquiring AWS and merging the two platforms

details.summary: Azure's growth strategy centers on enterprise customers already using Microsoft products. Enterprise agreements that bundle Azure with Office 365 and Windows licensing give Azure a sales channel that AWS and Google cannot match, making it the natural choice for Microsoft-centric organizations.
details.whyItMatters: Azure's enterprise bundling strategy explains its rapid market share growth. For organizations already invested in the Microsoft ecosystem, Azure offers the path of least resistance to cloud adoption.
takeaways: Azure bundles with Office 365 and Windows enterprise agreements
Microsoft's sales team reaches enterprises AWS salespeople cannot
Existing Microsoft skills transfer directly to Azure services

faq.question: Why do enterprises choose Azure over AWS?
faq.answer: Enterprises using Active Directory, SQL Server, and Windows find Azure's integration seamless. Microsoft enterprise agreements consolidate cloud spending with existing software licenses. The sales team understands enterprise procurement, compliance requirements, and long relationship cycles.

faq.question: Can you use Azure without Microsoft products?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Azure runs more Linux VMs than Windows. It supports open-source databases, containers, and programming languages. However, Azure's competitive advantage is strongest for organizations that also use Microsoft 365, Dynamics, and other Microsoft products.
